notes: §1985:XVI.3.3.4 SR1: a SORT in a non-independent segment names input and output procedures that each lie "Totally within non-independent segments, or" wholly in a single independent segment. SortBinder.SortBindFile resolves each INPUT and OUTPUT PROCEDURE range and CheckSegmentation asks Segmentation.CheckProcedures of each at its phrase (COBOL6877 at 85 for a fixed/independent mix); the witness INPUT PROCEDURE 10 THRU 60 from segment 0 is refused. Probes at --std 85 (work-rd-11): each procedure is checked on its own at its phrase (SortBinder.CheckSegmentation): s01 SORT in segment 0 with INPUT in 60 and OUTPUT in 70 accepted and ran (A B DONE), s02 SORT in 60 with INPUT in 60 and OUTPUT in fixed 20 ran (A B DONE), s03 SORT in 60 USING F1 OUTPUT in 70 refused COBOL6877, s07 SORT USING/GIVING (sequential files, no procedures) in 60 ran (A); c edition arm: a segment-number at 2002/2014/2023 is COBOL0902 and --permissive does not ask the rule (e01); a, d, f do not reach a procedure-placement rule. The procedures are the NAMED ones (docs/CONFORMANCE.md 3.8).
